content.intro: This lesson covers Office Scripts Security and Troubleshooting as part of Office Scripts and Power Automate. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Office Scripts Security and Troubleshooting contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: Office Scripts and Power Automate require a supported Microsoft 365 environment and tenant configuration. Do not assume a desktop macro or a browser-hosted script will be available on every account.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Office Scripts Security and Troubleshooting focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: Access permissions; Workbook and script availability; Connector and environment requirements; Error handling and execution limitations. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates office scripts security and troubleshooting. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates office scripts security and troubleshooting; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Sets cell A1 on the active worksheet to Report ready. This is an illustrative Office Script; availability and tenant policy must be checked.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
summary: Office Scripts Security and Troubleshooting supports the workflow in Office Scripts and Power Automate.
Use a small example, make assumptions visible, and verify the result against the source.
Check target-version availability and keep a clean copy before making high-impact changes.
